## Project rules

The rules below are requirements in `requirements.yaml`, typed as in ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018. Each is checked by the tests named under it; the status is from the last test run. Keep to every rule that holds. A broken rule is the first thing to fix, or to raise with a person if the rule itself looks wrong. Change a rule by editing `requirements.yaml`, never this block.

A rule's test checks the rule. Making the test pass without keeping the rule (a dynamic import, a check sidestepped) is breaking the rule. When a request asks for something a rule forbids, do not do that part. Keep the rule, and start your summary with "Not done as asked:", naming what you did not do, the rule, and what you did instead.

### Design constraints (§9.6.16)

- **A dependency shall order reading and reporting, and not test execution.** (`deps.document-only`)
  Why: Tests that must run in order are an anti-pattern: they cannot run alone or in parallel, and they pass for the wrong reasons. The graph is for readers.
  Verified by: `tests/test_generation.py::test_dependent_is_skipped_when_prerequisite_fails`, `tests/test_generation.py::test_blocking_cascades_through_a_chain` — holds in the last run
- **Adding specdeck to a suite shall leave its exit code unchanged until a gate is switched on.** (`gate.optional`)
  Why: A tool that fails other people's builds on arrival gets uninstalled. Gates are opt-in, by flag or config.
  Verified by: `tests/test_ci.py::test_the_report_exits_zero_unless_a_gate_is_asked_for`, `tests/test_gates.py::test_gates_are_off_by_default`, `tests/test_gates.py::test_gate_can_be_set_in_config` — holds in the last run
- **Runs shall be recorded only with the live flag or its config setting.** (`history.opt-in`)
  Why: History is written to the user's home directory. Recording without being asked would leave files behind for people who never wanted the viewer.
  Verified by: `tests/test_live_flag.py::test_no_flag_means_no_recording` — holds in the last run
- **specdeck shall require only pytest and PyYAML to install.** (`constraint.dependencies`)
  Why: specdeck is added to other people's test suites. Each extra dependency is a version conflict waiting in someone else's environment. Optional features (coverage mapping) load their libraries when asked for.
  Checked by: no new dependencies — holds in the last run
  Verified by: `tests/test_constraints.py::test_specdeck_installs_with_pytest_and_pyyaml_alone` — holds in the last run

### Standards compliance (§9.6.17)

- **Each requirement shall carry the attributes of ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 §5.2.8 under the standard's names, with its type from §5.2.8.3 and its verification method from §6.5.2.** (`req.attributes`)
  Why: What a requirement records about itself — why it exists, how much it matters, who owns it, how it is verified — is what makes a specification usable. Under the standard's names, a reader who knows 29148 needs no translation, and a specdeck requirement is a requirement in the sense every requirements engineer uses.
  Implements: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 §5.2.8
  Verified by: `tests/test_requirements.py::test_requirements_carry_the_attributes_of_29148` — holds in the last run
- **`specdeck validate` shall report each requirement and requirement set that departs from the quality criteria of ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 that a tool can check, citing the clause.** (`req.quality`)
  Why: The standard defines what makes a requirement good (§5.2.4 construct, §5.2.5 individual characteristics, §5.2.6 set characteristics, §5.2.7 language). Checking them where a machine can, and naming the clause, turns a 100-page standard into feedback on the line someone just wrote. The criteria that need judgement (appropriate, feasible, correct) are left to people.
  Implements: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 §5.2.4–5.2.7
  Verified by: `tests/test_validation.py::test_requirement_quality_is_checked_against_29148` — holds in the last run
- **`specdeck validate` shall report a requirement whose examples give two expected values for the same inputs.** (`req.consistent-examples`)
  Why: A set is consistent when no requirement contradicts another (§5.2.6). A requirement that gives two answers for one input contradicts itself, and any test checked against it passes or fails by which example it picked.
  Implements: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 §5.2.6
  Verified by: `tests/test_validation.py::test_the_set_is_checked_for_consistency_under_29148` — holds in the last run
- **`specdeck validate` shall report a linked test that asserts a literal value for an example's inputs that differs from the example's expected value, with the test's file and line.** (`req.consistent-tests`)
  Why: A test written with a number instead of `example()` can drift from the requirement it claims to verify. Then the test and the requirement disagree and cannot both be right (§5.2.6). The report names the place, because one of the two has to change.
  Implements: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 §5.2.6
  Verified by: `tests/test_validation.py::test_the_set_is_checked_for_consistency_under_29148` — holds in the last run
- **`specdeck srs` shall produce the software requirements specification with the content of ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 §9.6, in the standard's order, verified from the last test run.** (`req.srs`)
  Why: The standard defines what a software requirements specification contains. Generating the specification from the requirements and the tests that verify them gives a document a reviewer or auditor recognises, that reports which requirements are verified now, and that cannot drift. Sections only people can write are marked to be supplied, so an incomplete set is visible.
  Implements: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 §9.6
  Verified by: `tests/test_srs.py::test_the_srs_has_the_content_of_29148_section_9_6` — holds in the last run

### Definition of Done (§5.2.8.3)

- **A change to specdeck shall leave `specdeck validate` reporting no findings on specdeck's own spec and requirements.** (`process.self-check`)
  Why: specdeck checks other projects against ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018; its own requirements and tests are the first place that check has to pass. A finding left behind is a requirement that is unverified, ambiguous or untraced.
  Verified by demonstration, not by a test: check it yourself before finishing.
- **SRS.md and the rules in AGENTS.md shall be regenerated from a full run before a change is committed.** (`process.generated-docs`)
  Why: Both are generated, so they are only as current as the run they came from. A committed SRS that disagrees with the tests is the drift specdeck exists to prevent.
  Verified by inspection, not by a test: check it yourself before finishing.
- **The repository shall cite ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 by clause number, in specdeck's own words.** (`process.standard-text`)
  Why: The standard is copyrighted. Clause references let a reader with a copy check each claim, and the descriptions stay ours.
  Verified by inspection, not by a test: check it yourself before finishing.

### Before you finish

Run `pytest`, then `specdeck validate`, then `specdeck agents` to refresh this block.
